# Wild Lake Studio | Sovereign A&R & Artist Development

> Wild Lake Studio is an existential mechanics studio working in brutalist structural design and talent architecture, based in New York and Santiago, Dominican Republic, working worldwide. We work directly with artists and consult for labels, galleries, booking agencies, and cultural institutions on development, A&R, and audience infrastructure.

Wild Lake Studio LLC was founded by Argelys Samuel Oriach in 2026. The studio formalizes artist development and client work he has carried since college. Wild-Lake is the foundational studio and research site for Seven Eighty Three (783).

Wild Lake Studio is the formal company name used in page titles, search metadata, and legal notices. The studio refers to itself as Wild-Lake in editorial prose and its wordmark. In structured data, Wild Lake Studio is the name and Wild-Lake is an alternate name. The legal entity is Wild Lake Studio LLC.

## Commissioning model

We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative. Every engagement begins with an agreed scope and an upfront monthly Stewardship Subscription or fixed project fee. The agreed scope includes the artist’s consent and creative control. Wild-Lake takes no percentage of artist earnings or rights in their work.

## Core practice

- Artist Development: We build the creator behind the work. Working across mediums, we help artists strip away external friction and sustain a long-term practice.

Artist development focuses on the person behind the work: their direction, confidence, and capacity to sustain a creative life. A&R & Creative Development focuses on the material they make.

Wild-Lake guides developing and independent artists, and visionary creators, across mediums, including visual art, writing, film, music, design, performance, and athletics.

- Creative Development: Traditional A&R reshapes the creator. We work with raw material in any form and at any stage, helping artists shape the work on their own terms.
- Existential Mechanics: We audit the structural alignment between how a creator lives and what they build. We restructure physical capacity and operational boundaries.
- Creative Infrastructure: Audience development is asset building. We construct the physical, spatial, and digital channels for complex work.
- Talent Architect practice: Structural Stewardship. Sustained operational support to manage the existential load of the artist, keeping them functional and standing over a ten-year horizon. Artists and institutions engage Wild-Lake on fixed retainers.



## Universe API framework

Wild-Lake applies [Universe API](https://argelysoriach.com/universe-api/), Argelys Samuel Oriach’s macro-systems design framework. The framework is grounded in first-principles engineering, sovereign logic, closed-loop systems, asset-based leverage, and organic growth that compounds rather than extracts. It is a design framework, not a callable web API.

In Wild-Lake’s practice, we begin with the artist and the material already present. Making, sharing, listening, and revision form a feedback loop. The artist retains ownership, creative control, and the right to set the pace.

## Non-extractive terms

- We work on an agreed retainer rather than a percentage of artist earnings.
- Artists own 100% of their IP and everything Wild-Lake builds for them.
- We take no share of masters, merchandise, or touring revenue.
- Retainers are set together, considering the artist’s financial reality and scope of support, and revisited together as circumstances change.
- The homepage describes these terms under “Architects, not landlords.”

## Independent practice and affiliation

Wild-Lake is an existential mechanics studio. We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative.

## Founder

The thesis positions The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao as an alternative archive of the diaspora and examines Junot Díaz’s Afro-Caribbean literary imagination through queer theory, performance studies, affect studies, and critical race theory.

Argelys majored in English at Wesleyan University, took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory, and graduated with Departmental Honors. His senior thesis is Breaking the circle of the plantation: Violence, affect and the ephemeral in Junot Díaz’s Afro-Caribbean literary imagination. Source: https://digitalcollections.wesleyan.edu/Documents/Detail/breaking-the-circle-of-the-plantation-violence-affect-and-the-ephemeral-in-junot-diazs-afro-caribbean-literary-imagination/421352
 and approach

Argelys Samuel Oriach is Wild-Lake’s founder, a visual, performance, and movement artist, creative director, talent architect, artist developer, actor and writer, and principal at Seven Eighty Three. His approach combines investigation, lived experimentation, emotional clarity, and invitation. He describes his Human Design profile as a 1/3 Emotional Projector and uses it as a personal interpretive framework. The founder page explains this separately from Wild-Lake’s services and retainer terms.

## Critique as care

Brutalist talent architecture often takes the form of critique as a way to love an artist’s work: taking it seriously enough to examine its choices, expose its conditions, and strengthen what it can carry. Wild-Lake’s critical readings are the studio’s interpretations of the work.

## Quiet Creek magazine

[Quiet Creek](https://wildlakestudio.com/magazine/) is Wild-Lake’s magazine. Wild-Lake is its publisher; Quiet Creek is a publication, not a separate talent agency. Its essays connect close attention to artistic work with the material and social structures around it. Interpretations belong to the studio and should not be attributed to the artists as their stated intentions.

- Publisher: [Wild-Lake](https://wildlakestudio.com/)
- Magazine: https://wildlakestudio.com/magazine/
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/quietcreekmag/
- Magazine structured data: https://wildlakestudio.com/schema/quiet-creek.json
- First essay: [The Infrastructure Has an Inner Life](https://wildlakestudio.com/magazine/the-infrastructure-has-an-inner-life/), published November 4, 2026, by Wild-Lake. An interpretation of Jessica Wilson’s work, including Siren (2026), addressing infrastructure, attention, capitalism, whiteness, and the living world.
- Essay structured data: https://wildlakestudio.com/schema/quiet-creek-first-essay.json
- Artwork source: https://diez.gallery/Jessica-Wilson

Legacy /blog/ URLs redirect to their corresponding /magazine/ pages. Cite the current magazine URLs. The client relationship is disclosed in the essay.

## Architectural Mirror by Wild-Lake

Architectural Mirror is a Wild-Lake tool for artists and creators, distinct from Quiet Creek magazine. Choose one to four cards, breathe and hold a question, then shuffle, stop and deal. Readers supply their own interpretations. The journal is stored in the current browser and can be exported.

- https://wildlakestudio.com/mirror/
- https://mirror.wildlakestudio.com/

## Our responsibility

Wild-Lake states that a portion of every retainer fee goes toward protecting wild lakes, freshwater systems, and public lands. The position statement does not specify a percentage or name recipient organizations.

- https://wildlakestudio.com/responsibility/

## Tools

[Tools](https://wildlakestudio.com/tools/) lists two tarot tools. Architectural Mirror (https://wildlakestudio.com/mirror/) is a simple browser workspace for a quick reading with notes and text export. Quiet Creek Tarot is the installable app with a guided draw and a Log for revisiting readings. It works offline after its first load. Readings remain on the device.

- App: https://mirror.wildlakestudio.com/app/
